passages.title: My First School Radio Show
paragraphs: On Tuesday, I spoke on our school radio for the first time. My job was to introduce（介绍） a new song. Before the show, I practised reading my short script（讲稿） with a friend. I spoke too fast, so she asked me to slow down. When the red light came on, I took a deep breath and began. I made one small mistake, but I kept going. Afterwards, a younger pupil told me he enjoyed the song. I smiled. My voice could reach（传到） people I could not even see.

passages.title: The Pocket Money Notebook
paragraphs: I wanted a new set of coloured pencils, but I never seemed to have enough money. Dad suggested （建议） keeping a notebook. For two weeks, I wrote down everything I bought. I was surprised by the total（总额）. Small snacks and little toys cost more than I expected. I decided to save part of my pocket money each week. I still bought an ice cream sometimes, but I stopped buying things without thinking. After a month, I bought the pencils. I now understand the difference（区别） between wanting something and needing it.

passages.title: A Question Worth Asking
paragraphs: During a maths lesson, I did not understand the last step of a problem. Everyone else seemed ready to move on, so I kept quiet. Then our teacher asked if we had any questions. I slowly raised my hand. She explained the step again, using a drawing. Suddenly, it made sense. After class, two friends thanked me because they were confused（困惑的） too. I learned that asking a question does not mean I am a poor learner. Sometimes it is the most helpful（有帮助的） thing I can do for the whole class.

passages.title: The Chore We Swapped
paragraphs: My sister usually washes the dishes, and I fold（折叠） the clothes. One evening, we decided to swap（交换） our jobs. I thought washing dishes would be easier, but some rice stuck firmly to a bowl. My sister found folding a large bedsheet（床单） difficult too. We laughed and asked each other for advice. Soon, both jobs were finished. Now I understand why she sometimes needs more time at the sink. She understands my job better as well. Sharing the housework is useful, but learning to see things differently matters too.

passages.title: The Class Photograph
paragraphs: Our class photograph nearly went wrong. We were standing on the steps when the wind blew Mia’s hat away. Everyone turned to look, and the photographer（摄影师） missed（错过） his chance. Then someone sneezed（打喷嚏）, which made us laugh. Our teacher asked us to stand still, but even she was smiling. At last, we took a neat photograph. We also took a funny one with everyone waving. I like the second picture better. It reminds me of the sounds and laughter of that morning, not just the way we looked.

passages.title: A Screen-Free Afternoon
paragraphs: Rain kept us indoors on Saturday. My brother reached for his tablet, but I suggested（建议） spending an afternoon without screens. He was not keen at first. Then we found a box of old puzzles（拼图） under the bed. One puzzle had hundreds of pieces. We sorted them by colour and took turns searching for the edges（边缘）. Time passed quickly. We did not finish the picture, but we built most of a castle（城堡）. “Can we try again tomorrow?” my brother asked. I agreed. We had found a new way to enjoy our free time.

passages.title: The Plant on the Teacher’s Desk
paragraphs: Our teacher keeps a small plant on her desk. During the holidays, I offered to look after it. I thought more water would make it grow faster, so I watered it every day. Soon, some leaves turned yellow. Mum checked the soil（土壤） and found it very wet. She helped me let the extra water drain（排出） away. After that, I checked the soil before watering. The plant slowly looked healthier. When I returned it, I told my teacher what happened. Good care means understanding a plant’s needs, not simply doing more.

passages.title: An Interview with the Caretaker
paragraphs: For our class newspaper, I interviewed（采访） the school caretaker（校园管理员）. I thought his main job was opening the gate. He showed me his work list. He checks doors, fixes broken chairs and makes sure the playground is ready before we arrive. Sometimes he stays late to help after a school event. “What do you like best?” I asked. “Seeing everyone use the school safely,” he replied. I thanked him and took notes. The next morning, I noticed a repaired（修好的） bench. Now I knew whose quiet work was behind it.

passages.title: The Sound Map
paragraphs: Our music teacher asked us to make a map without drawing roads. Instead, we marked the sounds around our school. Near the kitchen, we heard bowls and spoons. Beside the sports hall, a ball bounced（弹起） again and again. Under a tree, leaves rustled（沙沙作响） in the wind. We closed our eyes for a moment and paid attention to each sound. Back in class, we compared（比较） our maps. They were all different because we noticed different things. I never knew our school could tell so many stories without using a single word.

passages.title: The Postcard That Took Its Time
paragraphs: My cousin sent me a postcard from a seaside town. For several days, I checked the letter box after school, but it stayed empty. Then the postcard finally arrived. The picture showed a lighthouse（灯塔） above the sea. On the back, my cousin described the salty wind and noisy birds. A message on a phone would be faster, but this card felt special（特别的）. I could hold it and see her handwriting（笔迹）. I put it above my desk. Some things are worth（值得的） waiting for, especially（尤其） when someone chooses them with care.

passages.title: How Shadows Tell the Time
paragraphs: On a sunny morning, our teacher placed a stick upright（竖直地） in the playground. We marked the end of its shadow（影子） with chalk. An hour later, we came back and made another mark. The shadow was in a different place. As the sun appears to move across the sky, shadows change their direction（方向） and length. Long ago, people used this idea to tell the time with sundials（日晷）. Our stick was not a perfect clock, but it helped us find out something interesting. Even a shadow can give us useful information.

passages.title: The Secret of a Thermos Flask
paragraphs: Dad takes hot tea to work in a thermos flask（保温瓶）. I wondered how it stays warm for so long. He explained that the flask has two walls with a special space between them. This helps slow down the movement（移动） of heat（热量）. The lid also helps keep the warmth inside. A flask can keep a cold drink cool for the same reason. It does not make the drink hotter or colder by itself. It simply slows the change. Now I make sure I close the lid（盖子） properly after using mine.

passages.title: Why Ducks Stay Dry
paragraphs: At the pond, I watched a duck dip its head into the water. When it came up, drops rolled off its back. Ducks spread oil over their feathers（羽毛） while cleaning them. The oil and the structure （结构） of the feathers help keep water away from their skin. Air among the feathers also helps keep them warm. I used to think a duck’s coat was like my cotton（棉布） T-shirt. Now I know it is different. Next time I visit the pond, I will look more closely instead of just watching the ducks swim.

passages.title: A Shell on the Beach
paragraphs: I found a beautiful shell during a walk on the beach. I was about to put it in my pocket when it moved. Two tiny claws（螯） appeared from the opening. A hermit crab（寄居蟹） was living inside! These crabs use empty shells to protect（保护） their soft bodies. As they grow, they need larger homes. I carefully put the shell back where I found it and stepped away. Soon, the little crab began moving again. What looked like a lovely thing to collect was actually someone’s home. I took a photograph instead.

passages.title: The Moon in the Daytime
paragraphs: One afternoon, I noticed the moon above the school roof. I thought it only appeared at night, so I asked our teacher about it. She explained that the moon is often in the daytime sky too. We see it when its position（位置） and the light make it visible （看得见的）. The moon does not make its own light. It reflects（反射） sunlight. That evening, I told Dad what I learned. Now I sometimes look up on my way home. The sky can surprise us even when the sun is still shining.

passages.title: A Bridge for Wild Animals
paragraphs: A busy road can make it difficult for wild animals to move between parts of a forest. In some places, people build special bridges covered with soil（土壤） and plants. These bridges give animals a way to cross above the traffic. Fences can help guide them towards the crossing. The bridges are different from those we use because they are designed（设计） for wildlife （野生动物）. Animals need time to get used to them. A road helps people travel, but we should also think about the creatures （生物） that need to travel through the same land.

passages.title: The Journey of a Parcel
paragraphs: When I ordered a storybook with Mum, I wanted it to arrive at once. She showed me how to track（追踪） the parcel（包裹）. First, someone packed the book and attached a label（标签）. Then the parcel travelled to a centre where workers sorted it with many others. A driver brought it to our neighbourhood the next day. I met him at the door with Mum and said thank you. A few clicks on a screen seemed simple, but many people worked together to deliver（递送） my book. I will remember that next time.

passages.title: Reading with Our Fingers
paragraphs: At a museum, I saw small raised dots beside a sign. They formed Braille（盲文）, a system that some people use to read by touch. Different patterns（图案） of dots stand for letters or other parts of a language. A guide gave us a sample（样本） card and showed us how to feel the dots gently. I could hardly tell them apart at first. Learning takes practice. Before leaving, I found another sign with raised dots near the lift. I began to pay attention to details that make public places easier for more people to use.

passages.title: The Market before Sunrise
paragraphs: My uncle sells vegetables at a market. One holiday morning, I went with him before sunrise. The streets were quiet, but the market was already busy. Uncle unloaded（卸下） boxes and checked the vegetables carefully. I helped put price cards beside the baskets. Soon, the first customers（顾客） arrived. One woman asked how to keep spinach（菠菜） fresh. Uncle answered while he weighed her vegetables. By the time most people began breakfast, he was working hard. I felt sleepy, but I also felt lucky to learn about a morning very different from my own.

passages.title: A Tune from an Old Instrument
paragraphs: At a cultural centre, I listened to an erhu player. The instrument had only two strings（弦）, but it made many beautiful sounds. The musician moved a bow（琴弓） between the strings and changed the notes with her fingers. One tune sounded cheerful; another sounded almost like someone crying. Afterwards, she let us ask questions. I asked how long she practised each day. “A little, but regularly（有规律地）,” she replied. I thought about my own music lessons. Skill does not appear all at once. It grows through careful practice, one small step at a time.

passages.title: The Shoes outside the Door
paragraphs: When I visited my friend Hana, I saw several pairs of shoes near the door. I began walking inside, but she gently showed me a pair of slippers（拖鞋）. “We leave our outdoor shoes here,” she explained. At dinner, I asked about other things her family liked to do. She was curious（好奇的） about my home too. We found many similarities （相似之处） and a few differences. I was glad I asked questions instead of making guesses. When we visit another home, being polite includes finding out what makes the people there feel comfortable.

passages.title: The Wrong Envelope
paragraphs: I wrote a thank-you card to my aunt and a funny note to my cousin. After sealing（封好） the envelopes（信封）, I noticed that one address was wrong. For a moment, I wanted to cross it out quickly and send both letters. Then I wondered if the cards were mixed up too. I carefully opened the envelopes. Sure enough, my aunt’s card was inside my cousin’s! I laughed, changed them and checked again. Since then, I double-check （复核） important messages before sending them. A few extra seconds can save time and prevent an awkward（令人尴尬的） mistake.

passages.title: The Umbrella We Shared
paragraphs: Heavy rain began just as school ended. I had an umbrella, but my friend Ben did not. We tried walking together under mine. At first, I held it over my own head, and his shoulder got wet. When he held it, my sleeve（袖子） got wet instead. We stopped, laughed and worked out a better way. I carried his bag while he held the umbrella between us. We walked slowly and stayed closer together. Sharing something is not always easy. Sometimes we need to adjust（调整） our actions so both people can benefit（受益）.

passages.title: The Rabbit’s Long Shortcut
paragraphs: A rabbit and a badger（獾） set off for the same hill. The badger followed the path, but the rabbit chose a shortcut（近路） through thick bushes. “I will arrive first,” he called. Soon, branches blocked his way. He turned left, then right, and finally reached a muddy ditch（沟）. By the time he found the path again, the badger was waiting on the hill. “Your road looked longer,” said the rabbit. “Yes,” replied the badger, “but I knew where it went.” The rabbit looked back at the bushes and shook his head.

passages.title: The Empty Seat at Rehearsal
paragraphs: Our class play was nearly ready when the pupil playing the king became ill. We had one afternoon to solve the problem. I knew his lines because I helped him practise, but I was only a stage helper. Our teacher asked me to try. My voice shook during the first rehearsal（排练）. The others waited patiently and helped me remember where to stand. By the end, I felt more confident （有信心的）. On the day of the show, I wore the paper crown （王冠） proudly. Sometimes a quiet helper must step forward when the team needs support.

passages.title: The Cake with No Winner
paragraphs: Three friends entered a cake-decorating（装饰） competition. Nora added bright flowers, Tim made a chocolate train, and May drew stars with icing（糖霜）. Just before the judging began, the organiser（组织者） announced a problem: the judge could not come. The children looked disappointed. Then May suggested（建议） sharing the cakes and describing what they liked about each one. Soon, everyone was talking and tasting. There was no winning cake, but every baker heard a kind comment. The organiser smiled. A competition（比赛） can be exciting, yet people can enjoy making things without always coming first.

passages.title: A Promise to the Little Ones
paragraphs: I promised to read a story to the younger pupils on Friday. Then my friends invited me to play football at the same time. I nearly said yes before remembering my promise. The younger children were already choosing a book for me. I told my friends I would join them later. During the story, a little girl asked why the dragon was lonely（孤独的）. Her question started a lively discussion（讨论）. I missed part of the game, but I enjoyed our reading time. Keeping a promise helped the children know they could trust（信任） me.

passages.title: The Message without a Name
paragraphs: Someone left a kind note on my desk: “Your drawing made me smile.” There was no name. I wanted to find the writer, but everyone simply smiled when I asked. All morning, I felt happier about my work. After lunch, I noticed that Lily’s poster was especially（尤其） clear and colourful. I wrote her a short note and left it beside her pencil case. I did not sign my name either. Perhaps kindness does not always need an audience（观众）. Sometimes a few honest words are enough to brighten （使愉快） someone’s day.

passages.title: The Jar of Small Successes
paragraphs: At the beginning of term, our teacher placed an empty jar（罐子） on a shelf. Whenever we learned something difficult, we could write about it and put the paper inside. My first note said, “I can spell Wednesday.” Later, I added one about finishing a long book. At the end of term, we opened the jar and read our notes. Some things seemed easy now, but they were once real challenges（挑战）. The jar showed us how much we could learn little by little. Small steps were adding up, even when we did not notice.

passages.title: What Makes a Good Listener?
paragraphs: I used to plan my reply（回答） while another person was still speaking. Once, my friend described a problem, and I interrupted（打断） with my own story. “Can I finish first?” she asked. I felt sorry and began listening properly. This time, I understood why she was upset（难过的）. A good listener does more than stay quiet. They pay attention, ask helpful questions and give the speaker time. Now I try to understand before offering advice. I do not always have an answer, but I can show respect（尊重） by letting someone’s words matter.
